scope: Architecture and capability-gap inventory for a Strata-owned prune-then-heal-then-quantize-then-verify pipeline for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as a later validation target. This receipt records pinned external facts, a local tooling inventory, the proposed stage order, and acceptance gates. It does not claim any built component, model download, pruning run, quantization run, LoRA run, or benchmark.

release.architecture: 512 routed experts per layer across 48 layers, 10 active per token
release.pruning: 256 of 512 experts retained per layer; 12,288 of 24,576 total
release.shard_2_note: per-layer n-gram table, IQ4_NL at 4.5 bpw, neither pruned nor searched, may be served from disk

vendor_benchmarks.oct17_update: SWE-bench Verified rose 75.60 to 79.20 and LiveCodeBench v6 86.28 to 87.43; only shard 1 changed

gsq.method: post-training scalar quantization; GPTQ second-order init then Gumbel-Softmax refinement of per-coordinate grid assignments and per-group scales; Lion optimizer with cosine schedule; per-layer shards offloaded to meta device so models larger than VRAM can be quantized; save_model.py reassembles an HF checkpoint
gsq.format_property: stays a symmetric group-wise scalar format, directly compatible with INT kernels and GGUF K-Quant deployment
gsq.listed_wrappers: LLaMA, Qwen3, Qwen3-MoE, Qwen3.5/3.6, Qwen3.5/3.6-MoE (hybrid attention, shared experts), Gemma-4, Kimi K2/K2.5
gsq.flash_next_wrapper_support: NOT listed; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with hybrid QSA/GDN/PLE layers is unverified against these wrappers

rco.method: budget-constrained optimization of a non-decomposable objective on a Riemannian manifold; softmax relaxation with tangent projection, retraction by binary search on a monotone cost map, and vector transport; discrete forward via Gumbel-STE with an exact multiple-choice knapsack solver; budget held to floating-point noise throughout
rco.pruning_entry: rco_search_prune.py -> mask.pt (per-layer expert keep/prune); groups are experts, options {keep, prune}, costs (0,1); routing weights scaled by STE survival masks
rco.materialize_entry: run_build_checkpoint.py -> pruned HF checkpoint (bf16, packed, or pruned)
rco.quant_entry: run_quantize.py builds a multi-bitwidth GPTQ database; rco_search_quant.py -> assignment.json per-layer bitwidth
rco.per_layer_budget_rationale: GGUF stores one expert count for the whole model, so every layer must retain the same count; RCO admits multiple simultaneous independent budgets, expressing the format constraint directly while keeping the KL loss joint across layers
rco.calibration_loaders: plain text wikitext2, c4, fineweb_edu; chat evol_codealpaca (code), tulu_math (math), answer-only masking; '+'-joined equal-count mixtures
rco.unfuse: src/unfuse.py splits fused 3D MoE experts into per-expert modules
rco.reported_efficiency: matches or exceeds EvoPress/EvoESAP evolutionary baselines at 3-16x lower wall-clock

flash_next_bf16_base.role: the RESMP-owned source checkpoint for any re-pruning or re-quantization; present and prunable

owned_deployment_chain.tools/strata_pack.py: pack build + verify under the rule decode(pack) == dequant_ggml(source) bit for bit, canonicalized over 757,139,840 blocks; the spec of record; satisfies the own-quantizer contract
owned_deployment_chain.tools/standard_imatrix.py: pinned RESMP-DEV calibration corpus 256x2048 with fixed dataset repo, revision, SHA-256
owned_deployment_chain.tools/make_profile.py: expert-profile ranking from --dump-routing traces; already supports --n-expert 256 for the pruned Coder
owned_deployment_chain.tools/bench_eviction.py: offline trace replay vs fill-only/LRU/LFU-decay/oracle eviction

prune_trace_signal.engine_flag: --dump-routing FILE records routed expert ids per layer and position for real workloads
prune_trace_signal.significance: we already capture activated experts on our own agent traffic; this is the calibration signal a REAP-style or RCO search needs, and it is workload-specific rather than the vendor's generic code+agentic+vision+spatial mixture

lora_training_infrastructure.present_on: Qwen3.8-27B (hidden 5120, 64 layers), not Flash-Next (hidden 2560, 48 hybrid QSA/GDN/PLE layers)
lora_training_infrastructure.artifacts: dozens of z-lab-Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-LoRA-r16 checkpoints plus a working CUDA trainer on the Prime cloud lane
lora_training_infrastructure.qat_path: MXFP4 QAT fake-quant with straight-through gradients already exists in the DSpark2 trainer branch (5f47153); measured ~11x BF16 full-replay cost, so QAT is a winner-only step not a sweep default
lora_training_infrastructure.gap: trainer targets 27B architecture; adaptation to Flash-Next's 48 hybrid layers with the PLE n-gram frozen is required
lora_training_infrastructure.absent_locally: peft, unsloth, GSQ, RCO not cloned

local_inventory.consumability: GSQ and RCO are Apache-2.0 and may be cloned and used as tools; the no-upstream policy forbids contributing to upstream, not using it. The own-artifact contract is satisfied because the runnable pack comes from our own BF16 base through our own bit-exact strata_pack.py with recorded source hash.

decision_rco_vs_reap.question: Is RCO nearly strictly better for our specific workloads, given we have compute?
decision_rco_vs_reap.answer: Largely yes for the expert-selection stage, with two qualifications; not unconditionally, and the choice is workload-calibration-driven, not method-brand-driven.
decision_rco_vs_reap.why_rco_is_stronger: REAP-style pruning ranks experts by a heuristic activation/importance score and keeps top-k per layer with no joint search. RCO optimizes the KL divergence of the FULL pruned model jointly across all layers under exact per-layer budgets, so it accounts for how removing an expert in one layer changes every other layer. The vendor reports it matches or exceeds evolutionary baselines (EvoPress/EvoESAP) at 3-16x lower wall-clock. With compute available, RCO is the better selection method.
decision_rco_vs_reap.qualification_1_budget_shape: RCO's headline advantage over a global-budget heuristic is largest when per-layer sensitivity varies. GGUF forces one expert count per layer, so a global budget cannot exploit that variation anyway; RCO still wins because its loss is joint, but the margin over a good per-layer REAP heuristic is a measurement question, not a certainty.
decision_rco_vs_reap.qualification_2_calibration_is_the_real_: Both methods are only as good as their calibration distribution. IST-DASLab calibrated on a generic code+agentic+vision+spatial mixture and explicitly invited feedback on capabilities absent from it. Our differentiation is not RCO-vs-REAP; it is calibrating either method on OUR --dump-routing agent traces. A REAP search on our traces can beat an RCO search on the vendor's generic mixture for our workload. Method and calibration are independent axes.
decision_rco_vs_reap.recommendation: Use RCO (rco_search_prune.py) as the primary selection method once a Flash-Next wrapper is confirmed, calibrated on a mixture built from our own agent routing traces plus evol_codealpaca. Keep a cheap REAP-style top-k-from-trace baseline as the control arm: it is nearly free from traces we already record, and it bounds what the expensive RCO search buys. Accept RCO only if it beats the REAP control on our held-out acceptance, not on the vendor's numbers.

stage_order.principle: prune in BF16, heal in BF16, quantize once at the end, verify bit-exactly. Healing a quantized artifact then re-quantizing loses most of the heal because re-rounding discards the adaptation. QLoRA restores nothing that pruning removed; it adapts the router and retained/shared weights to the smaller expert pool.

stages.name: calibration corpus build
stages.input: our --dump-routing agent traces + evol_codealpaca (code) + optional tulu_math
stages.output: trace-derived expert-importance signal and a calibration set for the search

stages.name: expert pruning
stages.method: RCO rco_search_prune.py -> mask.pt (256/layer exact budget) with REAP top-k-from-trace as control
stages.gate: exact 256 experts per layer; KL to unpruned on held-out calibration below threshold

stages.name: QLoRA heal (CPT)
stages.method: rank-8/alpha-16 LoRA short CPT, PLE n-gram frozen, Flash-Next hybrid-layer adaptation of the 27B trainer
stages.gate: router-loss and retained-weight recovery vs unhealed pruned on the same held-out set; no regression on the frozen n-gram path

stages.name: quantization
stages.method: GSQ Gumbel-Softmax scalar PTQ to a GGUF K-Quant-compatible grid (target ~3.5 bpw retained, matching the vendor), or RCO mixed-precision assignment.json
stages.gate: GSQ must confirm a Flash-Next wrapper or we write one; per-tensor type allocation recorded like the vendor rco-allocation.txt

stages.name: pack + verify
stages.gate: decode(pack) == dequant_ggml(source) bit for bit (verify is not optional); recorded source hash

stages.name: runtime validation
stages.method: Strata engine on a single 32 GB accelerator (V100 SXM2) with the 28.8 GB n-gram streamed from Optane/NVMe; then the two-P100 layer split
stages.gate: same-day control vs the vendor Coder IQ1_M at matched context; needle recall; a coding acceptance set; energy per token by tier

stage_order.optional_qat: A true fake-quant/straight-through QAT step is justified ONLY if the stage-4 GSQ BF16 candidate loses exact parity or paired live acceptance, per the existing architecture rule. The MXFP4 QAT path already exists in the DSpark2 trainer and is a winner-only step (~11x BF16 cost).

sequencing_qwen_first_then_deepseek.qwen_first: Executable now: we hold the BF16 base, the deployment chain, the routing-trace signal, and setup.py already registers the Coder family with --n-expert 256. The resident working set is 29.6 GB, testable on one 32 GB card.
sequencing_qwen_first_then_deepseek.deepseek_later: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash remains contracts-only in Strata (manifest, geometry, candidate selection; no runnable pack, quantizer, or CUDA backend). The same prune-heal-quantize-verify shape applies once a backend exists, but its 763B scale, 189.13 GiB Engram tables, and MXFP4/FP8 mixed storage make it a distinct, larger undertaking. Qwen validates the methodology; DeepSeek is the second target, not a parallel one.
sequencing_qwen_first_then_deepseek.engram_interaction: The n-gram/Engram table is excluded from pruning and from the quantization search in the vendor release and should stay frozen in ours; it is a lookup served from disk, and healing or re-quantizing it is out of scope for this pipeline.

acceptance_gates: Each stage produces a durable receipt with revision, dirty state, command, exit, calibration identity, and non-claims.
Pruning: exact 256 experts/layer, held-out KL below a pre-registered threshold, REAP control recorded alongside.
Heal: measured improvement over unhealed pruned on the same held-out set; frozen n-gram path unchanged.
Quantize: GSQ/RCO output must map to a GGUF K-Quant type Strata's kernels execute; per-tensor allocation recorded.
Pack: strata-pack verify bit-exact or the artifact does not exist.
Runtime: same-day matched control against the vendor artifact, named hardware, exact workload, and energy-per-token by tier; ordinary KL, offline replay, or throughput alone is not acceptance.
No default path changes: every stage is opt-in and preserves upstream defaults byte-identically until a measured decision changes them.
non_claims: No GSQ or RCO repo was cloned, run, or benchmarked; both are described from live-fetched README metadata only.
No pruning, heal, quantization, packing, or model run was executed this turn.
The SWE-bench Verified and LiveCodeBench figures are vendor-reported at xhigh reasoning and were not reproduced.
GSQ's Flash-Next (hybrid QSA/GDN/PLE) wrapper support is unconfirmed; the listed wrappers cover Qwen3.5/3.6-MoE, not Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
The local LoRA trainer targets Qwen3.8-27B, not Flash-Next; no Flash-Next fine-tuning ran.
Compute cost, wall-clock, and VRAM for each stage are not estimated here beyond the vendor's 3-16x efficiency claim for RCO.
This is an architecture and gap inventory, not built work; the stage order is a proposal with gates, not a completed pipeline.
